sourceProvisions: Division 8 provides standards for fences and walls.

Fence materials must be appropriate; walls need decorative finish; corrugated or sheet metal and injurious techniques are prohibited; wire fences must use chain-link and may not expose top points, wires, or prongs, subject to the unresolved barbed-wire provision.

Required-setback fences have finished-side, inward-support, maintenance-access, and visibility duties; street-facing planes over 100 feet require qualifying insets, openings, or architectural treatment.
Non-chain-link fences use the front, side/rear, waterfront, lot-type, retaining-wall, combined-height, and entry-component standards stated in this section.
Chain-link is prohibited Downtown and is subject to front-location, height, public-right-of-way, landscaping, recreation, vacant-lot, and public-landbank provisions.
Fences may not occupy specified rights-of-way/easements or enclose meters/manholes without authorization; utility-easement placement requires suitable access and preserves removal rights.
This section addresses pool enclosures, visibility, subdivision plans/perimeters, and Building Official approval of temporary construction fencing.
Fences must be maintained, may not lean or sag over ten degrees unless designed and permitted, and nonconforming-fence boards may be replaced if posts are not replaced.

At street/right-of-way and driveway/right-of-way intersections, the Sight Visibility Triangle figure depicts a triangle measured 20 feet along each applicable intersecting edge. Within it, no structure or landscaping may be installed other than a non-opaque fence not exceeding 30 inches in height. The text also protects views from 30 inches through eight feet above grade and provides for City Engineer approval.
A referenced landscape strip is outside the right-of-way and uses a solid hedge or a qualifying mix installed for coverage at maturity.
Defines relevant terms including easement, structure height, lot types, opaque, principal structure, property lines, right-of-way, and setbacks.
Building or repairing a barbed-wire fence adjacent to a street, alley, or sidewalk is unlawful; adjacent is not quantified in the reviewed extract.

Construction, demolition, modification, or renovation of a building or structure may not begin before a building permit is obtained. The Building Official receives the prescribed application and plans, the Community Development Coordinator reviews applicable development standards, and the Building Official reviews applicable building-code conformity.
On completion, the permit holder or agent must request a final inspection and any other inspection required by the permit.
